items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Jimmy has played trombone with Duke Ellington, Lionel Hampton and Ornette Coleman

ctx.x: Jeannie and Jimmy Cheatham have been creating swinging blues together since the late 50s, when they met in Buffalo, New York. Jimmy has played trombone with Duke Ellington, Lionel Hampton and Ornette Coleman, and taught jazz at Bennington College, the University of Wisconsin, and at the University of California at San Diego. His arrangements for the Sweet Baby Blues Band capture the Kansas City jump blues style and make the seven-piece band swing like Jay McShann and Count Basie.

Jeannie started as a classical piano student, but found a new sound to pursue after hearing Charlie Parker and Lester Young. She has accompanied Joe Williams, Big Mama Thornton and T-Bone Walker, and she was featured in the film “Three Generations of Blues” with Sippie Wallace and Ms. Thornton. This production was inducted into the Library of Congress’ 1997 Jazz Film Series along with the film, “Jeannie & Jimmy Cheatham and the Sweet Baby Blues Band.” They continue to add to their list of accomplishments from…
